Subject: Feature exception request: Greenfield Bank ask (per-tenant model pin + cache TTL)

Team —

Greenfield (prospect -> 80% close; see HubSpot deal GF-2026-0895) pushed a specific requirement in last week's technical review: they want the ability to pin a customer to a specific model variant at the API-key level and to set a per-tenant KV-cache TTL (to ensure cached completions aren't retained beyond their data retention window). They've said this is critical for their audit/compliance signoff.

High level:
- Ask: per-api-key model pin (immutable for the key) + per-tenant KV-cache TTL control exposed via account config
- Why: legal + audit want predictable model versioning + strict cache lifetime; avoids cross-tenant inference drift and simplifies their certification
- Customer impact: required for initial pilot + production rollout; will materially affect deal close and T&Cs (Greenfield has requested a written commitment)

What I need from you:
1) Quick feasibility check from Eng on major blockers and a rough engineering estimate (hrs / sprints)
2) Product stance on whether this can be shipped as an engineered exception (short patch) vs. roadmap item (Q4 planned)
3) Suggested minimum scope we can commit to in writing for the customer (so legal can draft SOW/appendix)

Attachments: I uploaded their one-pager and an excerpt of their SOW request (see attachments and Drive link).

I'm happy to sync, but given sales cadence we need an answer before EOD Wednesday (2026-08-04). Laura is aligned on tradeoffs and potential sweeteners (credits / extended pilot) if we can scope something pragmatic.

Thanks —
Soojin

Subject: Re: Feature exception request: Greenfield Bank ask (per-tenant model pin + cache TTL)

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick initial take from Eng:
- Per-api-key model pin is straightforward conceptually: we can add an api_key metadata field that resolves routing to a pinned model variant. Complexity depends on whether we support pinning for hosted variants only or also for dedicated/private variants (routing + compatibility checks). Estimate: 2-3 weeks for a minimal, behind-a-config feature to honor a pinned variant on request routing (including tests).
- Per-tenant KV-cache TTL is trickier because of how we surface cache policies today (global + per-model heuristics). To make TTL configurable per-tenant we need changes to the cache metadata, storage schema, and to the eviction/refresh logic. Minimal scoped implementation (configurable TTL that applies only to newly cached prefixes, no retroactive purge) — 3-4 sprints.

Questions for Product to decide scope:
- Can we accept an initial promise that TTL applies only to new cache entries (we will not retroactively purge existing cache)?
- Do we need to support automatic cross-check against their retention dashboard (audit) or is a documented TTL control sufficient?

I can flesh out a more detailed tech spec if we decide to move forward with an exception/accelerated workpackage.

- Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Feature exception request: Greenfield Bank ask (per-tenant model pin + cache TTL)

Thanks, Dev and Soojin —

Product POV: I think we can categorize this as an enterprise exception we can scope and deliver on an accelerated timeline, but we need to be explicit about expectations. Proposal:

MVP scope (what we can commit within 4 weeks, cross-functional):
- Per-api-key model pin: supported for hosted model variants only, enforced at routing time. No support for private/on-prem variants in MVP.
- Per-tenant KV-cache TTL: config via account settings that only affects newly written cache entries. No retroactive purge. Admin UI + API for TTL set to be added later (we can expose via admin flags / customer account config in the first cut).

Non-goals / caveats:
- No retroactive cache purge or guaranteed immediate purge for previously cached data.
- Not supported for dedicated/private deployments in MVP.
- We will surface documentation and a signed appendix but will not extend SLAs beyond normal terms unless Legal approves an SLA addendum.

If Sales wants a stronger commitment (retroactive purge / full private deployment support), that becomes a roadmap project (Q4+) and requires executive approval + pricing changes.

Action items:
1) Dev: rough implementation plan & risk register by EOD Thursday (2026-08-05)
2) Hannah: SRE/ops impact assessment (capacity / telemetry gaps)
3) Soojin/Laura: confirm what the customer is willing to accept in writing (appendix wording)

I'll tentatively block a POAP slot in the sprint plan if we get the green light.

Markus
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
